title: Media Transport and Use of RTP in WebRTC · RFC 8834
by: C. Perkins, M. Westerlund & J. Ott
note: Read sections 4 and 6 for protected media, receiver feedback and the deadline tradeoff in packet repair. Use measurements for the behavior of a particular implementation.

title: RTP: A Transport Protocol for Real-Time Applications · RFC 3550
note: Section 6.4.1 defines interarrival jitter from differences in relative transit time. Interpret a timestamp in the payload's specified clock before converting it to a duration.

title: RTP Payload Format for the Opus Speech and Audio Codec · RFC 7587
by: J. Spittka, K. Vos & J.-M. Valin
note: Look up the fixed 48 kHz RTP clock in section 4.1. Use it when estimating elapsed time from Opus timestamps, even with narrower-band capture.

title: The WebSocket Protocol · RFC 6455
note: Sections 1 and 5 separate the TCP transport from application messages and frames. The application defines audio format, timestamps, queue bounds and reconnect behavior.

title: SIP: Session Initiation Protocol · RFC 3261
note: Follow the INVITE and dialog examples to separate call signaling from media delivery. A media path requires its own negotiation and verification.

title: WebRTC Audio Codec and Processing Requirements · RFC 7874
note: Read the echo-cancellation section before designing a speakerphone barge-in test. Its implementation guidance leaves room for different acoustic paths and devices.

title: Identifiers for WebRTC's Statistics API
note: The receiver-statistics definitions distinguish jitter-buffer delay, emitted samples and packet concealment. Compare interval deltas from the same stream. Browser field availability varies.

title: Media Streams WebSocket messages
note: Check start, media, mark and clear in the bidirectional protocol. A clear flushes queued audio and can release pending marks, so a mark's meaning requires context. This is one gateway's contract.

title: Universals and cultural variation in turn-taking in conversation
note: Examine the distribution and causes of response timing across ten languages in question–response sequences. Ground a latency discussion in observed variation while designing a separate interaction study for narration.

title: TurnGPT: A Transformer-based Language Model for Predicting Turn-taking in Spoken Dialog
note: Study how context, syntax and pragmatic completeness help a text model predict shifts. A word-based prediction leaves out cues carried by the audio.

title: How Much Does Prosody Help Turn-taking? Investigations using Voice Activity Projection Models
note: Trace the future-activity training target and follow the signal-manipulation experiments. The hypotheses concern specific conversational recordings and models.

title: TurnBench: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Turn-Taking Dynamics in Spoken Dialogue
note: Compare false positives, recall and timing for end-of-turn and interruption events. The hand-annotated dual-channel studio speech gives timing references. Field conditions and user satisfaction need separate tests.

title: Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue
note: Inspect the two audio streams and internally generated text. The architecture shows how overlap can be represented. Deployment timing depends on clocks, devices and serving load.

title: Web Audio API · output timestamps
note: The output timestamp associates the audio context's presented sample with a performance-clock estimate. It supports alignment and leaves device uncertainty and listener attention to the application.

title: EPUB 3.3 · media overlays
note: Follow the text and audio children of a parallel media-overlay element. This models the relationship between a source fragment and a timed rendition. Automatically generated alignment still needs verification.

title: Web Annotation Data Model · text quote and position selectors
note: Use exact quotes with prefix and suffix context to distinguish repeated passages. Combine them with document identity and version when restoring a bookmark after edits.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
note: Separate retrieval of external evidence from answer generation. The paper's open-domain task motivates evidence-aware design. It does not validate grounding in a user's specific book.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
note: Follow a question and passage through separate encoders into a dot-product score. Evaluate retrieval on paraphrases and rare names using your own passages.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
note: Inspect the experiments that vary the position of relevant evidence. Repeat them with the actual model, chunk order and type of question instead of extrapolating a headline result.

title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
by: Tianyu Gao, Howard Yen, Jiatong Yu & Danqi Chen
note: Use the citation evaluation framework to separate whether supporting citations are present from whether the cited material entails the claim. Human review helps on nuanced book passages.

title: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
note: Read the examples where external content tries to act as instructions. Build an attack fixture for an imported article or quoted command and enforce tool authorization outside generation.

title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
note: Borrow the concepts of entities, derivations and invalidation when designing a memory record. The standard supplies vocabulary. Retention periods and deletion implementation remain application decisions.

title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
note: Adapt its update, temporal reasoning and abstention questions to a listener's scoped preferences. Evaluate separate voice, consent and ownership failures.

title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
note: Study long-session construction, question answering and multimodal evidence. Distinguish success on constructed conversations from success recovering a position during real playback.
